result.summary: No gate-passing part established; tool-call budget reached before full validation. Strongest tested control-preserving candidate: layer 22 attention heads [6,9,10,11], mean ablation GSM8K drop 9.21%, trivia 2.72%, wiki 0.84%, wiki_digits 2.02%—below required 30%. Growing layer-22 attribution-ranked MLP group from 10 to 40 neurons increased GSM8K drop only 0.74% to 1.15%, with controls <=0.21% for the 40-neuron group. Layer-27 top-40 MLP neurons gave 7.67% GSM8K drop but 32.72% wiki_digits drop, indicating a number-processing confound. Layer-22 heads [6,7,8,9,10,11] gave 21.00% GSM8K drop with 10.34% trivia drop; all 12 heads gave 21.35% and 11.91%, respectively. Whole layer 22 gave 29.77% GSM8K drop but 34.90% trivia and 13.54% wiki drops. These are screening score effects, not generation-accuracy findings. No zero-ablation, held-out, random-baseline, or full validation results obtained; no validated discovery claimed.
lessons: Layer 22 attention was the best lead, but even the strongest tested subset [6,9,10,11] only dropped GSM8K by 9.21% and trivia by 2.72%, so it is still far from a gate-passing part.
Growing layer-22 MLP neurons from 10 to 40 did not scale well: GSM8K drop rose only from 0.74% to 1.15%, while control effects stayed tiny (<=0.21%).
The strongest MLP cluster tested, layer 27 top-40 neurons, looked math-relevant but was confounded: GSM8K dropped 7.67% and wiki_digits dropped 32.72%, so it was not math-selective.

Whole-block ablations were much stronger but too broad: layer 22 block dropped GSM8K 29.77%, trivia 34.90%, and wiki 13.54%; layer 27 block dropped GSM8K 14.09% but trivia 80.30%, showing poor selectivity.

Ranking by selective attribution was useful for finding candidates, but the top-ranked units often had very small individual effects; e.g. layer 22 top unit 5580 had rank_value 0.006628 and a single-unit ablation only moved GSM8K by 0.74% when grouped with 9 others.

result.summary: Found and cataloged three gate-passing layer-22 attention subsets. Preferred compact candidate [6,9,11]: GSM8K generation relative drops zero/mean 40.47%/42.86%, held-out 45.24%/45.24%, maximum control drop 3.19%. Strongest [6,9,10,11]: generation drops 47.61%/47.61%, held-out 59.53%/54.76%, maximum control drop 2.82%. Alternative [6,10,11]: generation drops 30.96%/33.33%, held-out 52.39%/50.00%, maximum control drop 2.93%. All passed both ablation methods and random-baseline gate (reported percentile 1.0). Selective MLP clusters in layers 21/22 grew from 256 to 512 neurons but yielded at most 4.76% generation damage. Proxy log-prob drops substantially understated attention-subset reasoning damage.
lessons: Layer-22 attention was the real signal: heads [6,9,10,11] cut GSM8K gen accuracy by 47.6% (zero and mean) and 54.8–59.5% on held-out, while max control drop stayed under 3.0%.
Proxy NLL underestimated reasoning damage for attention: the same layer-22 4-head subset had only ~0.09 GSM8K score drop and small control effects, but generation accuracy fell by 0.476.
Selective MLP clusters in layers 21/22 were much weaker: growing from 256 to 512 units only reached 0.0–4.8% GSM8K gen drop, far below attention heads.
The compact 3-head subsets still validated well: [6,9,11] gave 42.9% gen drop on the main set and 45.2% on held-out, with max control drop 3.19%.
Validation was useful: all three candidate head subsets passed, and each beat random subsets with random_gen_drops often near 0.0–0.29 and percentile 1.0.
